claims.finding: Pyxis has a live, never-consummated equity offering on file -- F-1 accepted 2026-05-27, F-1/A 2026-06-29, a free writing prospectus on 2026-07-21 and a further F-1/A two days later on 2026-07-23 -- and no 424B of any kind appears in the filings index through the 2026-08-30 sweep, meaning the deal was actively marketed in July, stalled, and now sits as unresolved supply over a $55-65m market cap that has run +137% off its 52-week low into an after-hours print.
claims.why_not_priced: The only sentiment source in the capture -- 90 StockTwits messages spanning 2025-11-21 to 2026-08-30 -- never once mentions an offering, an F-1, dilution or a prospectus for PXS, while the same thread carries two long verbatim reposts of TOP Ships withdrawing its own $10m F-1 on 2026-05-15, so this audience reads shipping-sector registration news closely and has still not connected it to the name it is long. The tape says the same: through the FWP marketing window the stock rose (4.46 on 07-20 to 4.53 on 07-23 on 6,700-34,300 shares a day) rather than gapping or building volume, which is not what a market discounting imminent dilution looks like, and it has since gone on to make new highs. If the overhang were priced, the run-in would have stalled at the FWP, not accelerated 55% off it.
claims.independence: The tape in the same capture points the same way from a different file: quote.json shows 5.40 on 2026-08-31 against a 6.22 baseline spot on 2026-09-04, a +15% four-session sprint into the print with no captured news to explain it -- exactly the strength into which a stalled small-cap deal gets priced. Retail's blindness to the filing is corroborated at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/top-ships-announces-sale-newbuilding-153000900.html (docs/a49e57c3ffce0ad6e30a4576506d2fcbfb3b18dd.txt, 2026-07-28), which shows the thread tracking peer capital-markets action in detail on the same days the PXS F-1/A and FWP were filed.

claims.finding: The baseline's 2.33% expected move is built from eight 6-Ks that are mostly not results filings: the corpus confirms the actual Q4/FY2025 release was 2026-03-05 before the open, yet 2026-03-05 appears neither in the baseline's reaction history nor anywhere in filings.json, while three dates that are in the history (2026-02-02, 2026-04-10, 2026-04-24) are non-results 6-Ks -- so the event base rate for this name is mis-specified and, at 65% annualised realised vol (4.1% per day), understated to below the width of an average session.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/a49e57c3ffce0ad6e30a4576506d2fcbfb3b18dd.txt, message dated 2026-03-04T20:49:18Z quoting 'We will issue our unaudited results for the fourth quarter and year ended December 31, 2025, before the market opens in New York on Thursday, March 5, 2026'; cross-checked against filings.json, which jumps from 2026-02-02 to 2026-04-01 with no 6-K on or near 2026-03-05
claims.why_not_priced: This is not a claim about what the market missed but about what my own anchor gets wrong, and it is load-bearing for the width of my number rather than its sign. It is unpriced only in the sense that the printed base rate any screen would compute from EDGAR 6-K text-matching -- the same heuristic the baseline used, which its own event_plausibility block flags as a 51-day cadence that cannot be an earnings cadence -- systematically understates this name's event vol. If a 2.33% reaction were the right expectation, the stock would not be running 4.1% a day in ordinary sessions.
claims.independence: Shares the StockTwits document with finding 1's why_not_priced clause, so the two are not fully independent and the scorer should collapse them to the larger residual; the independent leg here is filings.json itself, which is a different file and whose gap at 2026-03-05 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1640043/000149315226014641/form20-f.htm is the next filing after 2026-02-02) is what makes the mis-specification checkable rather than asserted.
